operation_details.item: The user has chronic dry eye from screen use and should follow blink reminders, lighting adjustments, and clinician guidance.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: I see you're preparing for a multi-day hackathon next week. Have you started planning your setup and schedule to stay comfortable and productive?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Yes, I've got my laptop and external monitor ready, but I'm worried about eye strain. I usually code for hours without a break.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: That's a real concern. For long coding sessions, I'd recommend taking a 5-minute break every 25–30 minutes, and using the 20-20-20 rule: every 20 minutes, look at something 20 feet away for 20 seconds. Also, make sure your room lighting isn't too harsh or too dim.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Good points. I should also mention that I have chronic dry eye from extensive screen use; I should be reminded to blink regularly, use appropriate lighting, and follow my eye clinician's guidance.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Absolutely, following your eye clinician's advice is crucial. I won't suggest any new treatments, but I can help you structure reminders for blinking, adjusting lighting, and hydration. For the hackathon, you might set a timer for blink breaks and keep a water bottle nearby.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: That sounds helpful. I'll set up a Pomodoro timer with blink reminders and adjust my monitor brightness based on the room's ambient light.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Great plan. You could also position your screen slightly below eye level and use a matte screen filter to reduce glare. And don't forget to blink fully—sometimes we do partial blinks when focusing.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: I'll try that. I also have some lubricating eye drops my clinician recommended, so I'll keep those handy.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Perfect. Since you're already following your clinician's guidance, you're on the right track. For the hackathon, consider alternating between standing and sitting, and maybe use a blue light filter after dark. Would you like me to help you set up a quick checklist?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: A checklist would be great. I'll also make sure to take a short walk during longer breaks to keep my blood flowing.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Excellent. Here's a quick checklist: 1) Pomodoro timer with blink reminders, 2) proper lighting (warm, indirect), 3) screen at eye level, 4) hydration, 5) lubricating drops as needed, 6) stand periodically. You've got this!

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Thanks, that covers everything I need. I'll start implementing these tomorrow.
